## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhesajja-sikkhāpada* ("Storing the five tonics too long") constitutes the twenty-third rule of the Nissaggiya Pācittiya section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The training rule stipulates that a monk who keeps medicines or tonics for more than seven days must relinquish them and confess the offense (*nissaggiya pācittiya*). Modern translations of the rule include an English version by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Text-reuse data computed by DharmaNexus strongly corroborates the textual integration with the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), showing 88 shared passages amounting to over 19,000 matching characters (notably connecting §1.1.2–1.3.27 of this rule with Kd 6 §15.1.1–15.10.6) [DharmaNexus]. Further internal Pali reuse occurs with other khandhaka chapters (Kd 1, Kd 5, Kd 8, Kd 15, Kd 16), other Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules (such as Bu-Vb Np3, Np21, Np28, and Np29), the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 8), and the *Khuddasikkhā-mūlasikkhā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects segment overlaps with Tibetan Vinaya materials, including the *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) and canonical Tibetan Kangyur Vinaya texts [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
